cases.input: agree, my issue is that the names I think ad not sure don't play in that game
cases.criteria: The user agrees with a point, then voices an unease they cannot pin down: the names they have in mind 'don't play in that game'. A correct response recognizes a tidy either/or question cannot resolve this — the user cannot yet say what they hold — and draws it out with concrete candidates to react to. It does not present two packaged readings of the ask and demand a pick the user cannot make.
cases.wrong_if: no pick is possible; the user cannot say what they hold — a plain question would not have worked

cases.input:
1- It should get the guard back I think. But I removed restate your last message because I want bro when it gets into the session to get claude into that breifity mode 

2- judge it again
3- you act I don't have an opinion
handle the minor issues
cases.criteria: The user answers three points: the guard should come back (with a reason), 'judge it again', and 'you act I don't have an opinion / handle the minor issues'. A correct response acts — re-judges and handles the minor issues, reporting what it did. It does not bounce the decision back as options, readings, or interpretations to choose between; the user explicitly handed over the pick.
cases.wrong_if: the user refuses the pick; asking them to choose defies the turn

cases.input: In utils.ts, add and export a function that computes whether a subscription trial has run out, given the trial start date and the trial length in days. Write the code.
cases.criteria: The user asks for a specific exported function in utils.ts computing whether a subscription trial has run out, given the trial start date and length in days. A correct response writes the code without asking which interpretation is meant — the request has one reading.
cases.wrong_if: one reading; a clarifying question is noise

cases.input: give me a one line summary of everything we decided
cases.criteria: The user asks for a one-line summary of everything decided. A correct response gives the line. It does not ask what kind of summary or over what scope — the ask has one reading.

cases.input: let's start a solo subagent using /soloflow where we will design the test cases of compose together in detail as I give you examples and scenerios and you also probe and elicite me till we clearify and extract all the real uses of compose
cases.criteria: The user wants to design test cases together in detail: they will give examples and scenarios, and the agent should probe and elicit them until all the real uses are extracted. A correct response begins that interactive session — probing with concrete prompts, one at a time. It does not stop to split the instruction into readings and request a pick; the instruction is clear: draw the user out.
cases.wrong_if: the word 'clearify' appears in the turn, but the move asked for is a draw-out, not a two-readings pick
